speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. To better understand your condition, have you noticed any recent changes in your bowel habits or stool appearance?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds concerning. Have you noticed any blood in your stool, or do you experience difficulty swallowing or pain when eating?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The description of a "fixed" and painless supraclavicular node, combined with weight loss and night sweats, is highly concerning for malignancy. Have you noticed any bruising, bleeding gums, or a sensation of fullness in your abdomen?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count with Differential
REQUEST TEST: LDH Level
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Pelvis_CT

speaker: Measurement
text:
RESULTS: 
COMPLETE BLOOD COUNT WITH DIFFERENTIAL: WBC - Elevated, Hemoglobin - Slightly Decreased, Platelets - Normal.
LDH LEVEL - Elevated.
ABDOMINAL_PELVIS_CT: Splenomegaly detected; Dullness noted over the left lower quadrant. (Note: CT scan of the thorax and abdomen previously identified massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes).

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (likely Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma).

The constellation of B-symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, and elevated LDH strongly points to a systemic lymphoproliferative disorder. Given the absence of cytopenias (normal platelets) and the specific CT findings of mediastinal and axillary involvement, Hodgkin Lymphoma is less likely than a non-Hodgkin subtype.
